title: kill the root, with a root in the divisor
source: DESIGN.md §8.5's row 'sqrt(u) inside f(.) -> u = t^2'; the owner's answer of 2026-09-24 pinning sqrt_nonneg (p1_expected E49)
statement: Evaluate the definite integral of 1/(1 + √x) from 0 to 4.
notes: Installation owes the divisor 1 + sqrt x # 0 on [0, 4]. It closes by the linear method with sqrt_nonneg's sqrt x >= 0 (E49): (-(1 + sqrt x)) + sqrt x = -1. Before the owner's answer it was admitted, tagged none.
After x := t^2 the divisor is 1 + sqrt(t^2) # 0 on [0, 2], closed the same way, and sqrt_sq turns it into 1 + t.
ftc checks by field: 2 - 2/(1 + t) is 2t/(1 + t) where 1 + t # 0, which the range gives. ln(1 + 2) and ln 3 are one atom (§6.2), so the close is ring's.
